locator: §3.1, BHK-interpretation, 'According to the BHK-interpretation this statement holds intuitionistically if'
interpretation: Attribution reading: the entry reports that, by the BHK-interpretation, A ∨ ¬A holds intuitionistically if the Creating Subject knows a proof of A or a proof that A cannot be proved, in line with the BHK clause that a proof of A ∨ B is a proof of A or a proof of B. Taken in the direction needed: a proof of p ∨ ¬p at a stage is a proof of p or of ¬p there. The claim records the intuitionist position the encyclopedia reports (Brouwer, Heyting), not a thesis of the entry's author. Secondary witness: no primary text is pinnable (DUMMETT-EOI).
